hypothesis: The model's next-step predictor transfers to systems outside its training distribution (lower mass ratios, higher eccentricities). If so, it encodes something law-like rather than shortcuts fitted to the training range.
expected_if_true: In both seeds, val_mse_ratio stays < 1 on every two-body OOD eval set (mass_ratio [0.01, 0.1]; eccentricity [0.5, 0.8]) and is within 10x of the in-distribution ratio (about 0.01). The force and accel_step probes still beat their controls by >= 0.1 at the final checkpoint.
expected_if_false: On at least one two-body OOD set, val_mse_ratio is >= 1 in both seeds, or more than 10x worse than in-distribution while in-distribution stays below 0.05. That would mean the predictor depends on the training range of m2 or e. The three-body set is reported as exploratory: a ratio >= 1 there is expected and does not refute the hypothesis on its own.
